info.title: IT Support Hub - Ticket API
info.description: Ticket listing and creation documented from the supplied ExternalTicketController::index and ::store. POST /api/ticket and bearer authentication are retained from prior integration documentation. GET /api/ticket is assumed to map to index; confirm it against routes/api.php before use. Route/middleware configuration, model serialization, and TicketService internals were not supplied. Example IDs are placeholders. No production request was submitted.

get.summary: Get tickets assigned to a user
get.description:
Lists tickets with an assignees relation whose user_id matches assigned_id. Results are ordered by created_at descending, then internal id descending. No status, priority, board, or date filters are implemented in this controller. assigned_id must reference an existing user; index does not apply the active-user/role rules used by create-ticket assignee validation. No matches returns HTTP 200 with an empty data array. Checklist items and attachments are not included in this listing. The controller does not show authorization checks restricting which assigned_id callers may query; access depends on deployed middleware/policies.

Route assumption: GET /api/ticket maps to ExternalTicketController::index. Confirm routes/api.php; the controller alone does not define the URL. Authentication remains the existing Support Hub bearer scheme. Response examples use illustrative IDs and status values, not live records.

post.description:
Creates a production ticket. Requester lookup uses normalized lower-case email. If no requester exists, the controller creates an active, verified viewer account with a random password and change_password=1; an existing requester phone is updated when a non-empty different phone is supplied. The ticket source is external_api. Defaults: priority=medium, ticket_type=request. Choose JSON without files or multipart/form-data for uploads. Do not automatically retry an uncertain result: TicketService idempotency was not provided, and an error after persistence may still mean a ticket exists.

### Board and checklist
- `board_id`: optional active board ID, for example `1`. Alternatively use `board_slug`; do not supply both non-empty values. Omit both for backlog.
- `checklist`: optional list of up to 50 items. Each item requires `content` (nonblank, maximum 500 characters), with optional `is_completed` (default false) and `assigned_to` (active eligible user ID or null).
- Ticket and checklist assignees must have access to the selected board. All example IDs are placeholders.

The default JSON example includes board_id and checklist. For file uploads, choose multipart/form-data and use `board_id`, `checklist[0][content]`, `checklist[0][is_completed]`, and `checklist[0][assigned_to]`; increment the index for additional items.

ticketBearer.description: Support Hub API token; paste token only. Retained from existing integration; authentication middleware was not included in the supplied controller.

category_id.description: Existing active category ID. Its department must match department_id unless the category has no department.

board_id.description: Existing active board ID. Use instead of a non-empty board_slug. Omit or null both selectors for backlog.

assignee_id.description: Optional active admin, super_admin, or technician user ID. Must have access to the selected board when one is supplied.

board_slug.description: Existing active board slug. Use instead of a non-empty board_id.

source_app.description: Non-empty value is merged into request_context.source_app, overriding the same context key.

external_reference.description: Non-empty value overrides request_context.external_reference and is echoed in the response. No idempotency guarantee is shown by the controller.

request_context.description: Laravel array validation accepts a JSON object or array. Metadata passed to TicketService; non-empty source_app and external_reference overwrite corresponding keys. Empty context becomes null.

checklist.description: Optional sequential list of at most 50 items. Omitted/null becomes an empty checklist. Only content, is_completed, and assigned_to are allowed per item.

CreateTicket.description: Supply either a non-empty board_id or board_slug, not both. Both may be omitted or null for backlog. A category with a department must match department_id; a category with no department is allowed. Active records are required. Non-null ticket/checklist assignees must be active admin, super_admin, or technician users and have access to the selected board. Explicit null for one board selector does not conflict with the other.

attachments[].description: Up to 10 files, each at most 10240 KB (10 MiB). Allowed types: jpg, jpeg, png, pdf, doc, docx, txt, webp. Server validates MIME/file type, not just filename.

checklist[0][content].description: First checklist item. Repeat indexed fields with [1], [2], etc., up to [49] for more items.

checklist[0][is_completed].description: Optional first-item completion flag; defaults to 0.

request_context[page].description: Example context key. Use request_context[your_key] to send other metadata fields.

CreateTicketMultipart.description: Supply either a non-empty board_id or board_slug, not both. Both may be omitted or null for backlog. A category with a department must match department_id; a category with no department is allowed. Active records are required. Non-null ticket/checklist assignees must be active admin, super_admin, or technician users and have access to the selected board. Explicit null for one board selector does not conflict with the other. Nested form fields use PHP bracket notation, not JSON strings. The interactive example exposes checklist index 0 and context key page; clients may send additional indices/keys. Omit optional fields rather than sending empty strings for numeric fields.

assignee_id.description: First ticket assignee user ID, or null.
